The given figure is a demonstration of an experiment to show that carbon dioxide is essential for photosynthesis. What is the substance X, kept in watch-glass?

(The figure shows a destarched potted plant placed inside a sealed bell jar. A watch-glass containing substance X is kept on the floor of the jar beside the pot, so that any gas it absorbs is removed from the air around the plant.)

The given graph shows changes in the air pressure of lungs during breathing. What causes the change in air pressure during period X?

(The figure is a graph with air pressure in the lungs in K(Pa) on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis. Period X is at the start of the time axis: the curve first falls below the starting level to a trough, then rises to a peak above it, then settles back. Period X marks the initial fall — the pressure in the lungs decreasing.)

options.label: A
options.text: Movement of ribs downward and inward

options.label: C
options.text: Relaxation of the external intercostal muscles

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease in the volume of the lungs

stem:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the given figure?
1. The parts labelled as Q and R carry blood having low oxygen concentration.
2. The parts labelled as P, Q and R carry blood having low oxygen concentration.
3. The blood flows out of the heart through blood vessel Q when ventricle contracts.
4. The blood is flowing out of the heart through blood vessel Q when atria contract.

(The figure is an external view of the human heart. P points to a vessel at the top of the heart, Q points to a large vessel arising from the heart on its anatomical-left side, and R points to a vessel on the anatomical-right side.)

Mohit prepared temporary mount of a leaf peel and drew the following diagram. The missing part in the diagram is:

(The figure is a leaf-peel diagram of a stoma. Two kidney-shaped guard cells flank a central stomatal pore; both are labelled. The surrounding outer cells that enclose the guard cells are left unlabelled — this is the missing part to be identified.)

Four students, A, B, C and D, make the records given below, for the parts marked 'X' and 'Y' in this diagram.

(The figure is a leaf-peel stoma: two kidney-shaped guard cells, each dotted with chloroplasts, surround a central pore and are embedded in epidermal cells. Label X points to one of the kidney-shaped guard cells; label Y points to the central pore between the two guard cells.)

| Student | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| A | Stoma | Guard cell |
| B | Guard cell | Stoma |
| C | Epidermal cell | Stoma |
| D | Stoma | Epidermal cell |

The correct record, out of these, is that of student :

In the diagram of stomata shown below, the labeling of four students was tabulated by the teacher in the table given below. Whose labeling was correct?

(The figure is a leaf-peel stoma. Labels I, II, III and IV point to four parts: the nucleus inside a guard cell, the central stomatal pore, a surrounding epidermal cell, and the cell wall.)

| Student | Nucleus | Stoma | Epidermal cell | Cell wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | IV | III | II | I |
| B | II | IV | I | III |
| C | I | II | III | IV |
| D | III | I | IV | II |
